conviction_note: Near-zero on both measurements: the sell side cut targets and full-year EPS into the print and the stock de-rated about 12% from early September against about 6% for KRE, so the bar looks lowered (a mild positive), while Q2 credit was worsening (NCOs 0.80% vs 0.63%) and is the likely reason for the cuts (a mild negative, shrunk because the short is about 10 days to cover). The findings net to -0.1 and the scaled number (p_up 51 x abs 4.5) is +0.09. The searcher's web-search budget for this turn was used up before the hunt began, so the evidence comes from direct fetches of EDGAR, Yahoo, finviz, MarketBeat and StockTitan only, and no peer prints or SBA weekly series could be reached.
bar: Q3 2026 diluted EPS about $0.66 (finviz 'EPS next Q', fetched 2026-10-21, https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=LOB). This is one source, with no second agreeing estimate and no company guide (the Q2 release gives no outlook: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1462120/000146212026000053/lob-20260722exx991.htm), so every size is capped small. FY2026 EPS consensus is $2.96 per MarketBeat on 2026-10-14 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/analyst-live-oak-bancshares-nyse-lob-stock-gets-price-target-cut-from-cantor-fitzgerald-2026-10-14/), down from $3.07 on 2026-10-07 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-live-oak-bancshares-nyse-lob-stock-price-down-72-heres-what-happened-2026-10-07/). H1 actual is $1.34 ($0.60 + $0.74).
positioning_check: Short float 6.12% and short ratio 9.91 days (finviz quote page, fetched 2026-10-21; settlement date not shown, presumably the late-September/early-October FINRA print; https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=LOB). Ten days to cover on about 231k shares a day is a heavy short relative to liquidity, so negatives are shrunk. The Nasdaq short-interest API returned 503. Options are unusable (11 contracts open interest in total, no two-sided ATM quote), so there is no skew. Insiders own about 22.4% and institutions about 64% (MarketBeat 2026-10-07). Tape: 20d -5.07%, 5d +2.3%, -19.5% from the 52-week high.

findings.finding: The sell side cut price targets in the two weeks before the print: TD Cowen $49 to $44 (Buy) on 2026-10-05, Piper Sandler $46 to $38 (Neutral) on 2026-10-07, Cantor $45 to $41 (Neutral) on 2026-10-14. FY2026 EPS consensus fell from $3.07 to $2.96 between 10-07 and 10-14, and LOB fell 6.1% on 10-07 (36.49 to 34.26, on 434k shares, about 1.9x average) while KRE fell 1.7%. Since 2026-09-03 the stock has gone from $39.56 to $35.21 (-11%), against KRE from 74.87 to about 70.4 (-6%). So the EPS bar and the price were both lowered into a print where LOB beat on 3 of its last 4 quarters ($0.74 vs $0.64, $0.60 vs $0.54, $0.95 vs $0.56).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The EPS beat/miss has set the sign on recent prints. Q2 2026 beat by $0.10 and the stock rose +3.9%; Q1 2026 beat by $0.06, +3.28%; Q4 2025 beat by $0.39, +4.51%; Q3 2025 missed by $0.03, -3.29% (MarketBeat estimate history https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/LOB/earnings/ against baseline moves).
findings.why_not_priced: The cuts themselves are public and the 10-07 drop priced them, so the part that may not be priced is how far the bar was lowered. If the market expected a beat against the lowered number, the stock would have recovered some of the 10-07 gap into the print. It has not: it is still $35.21 against $34.26 at the 10-07 close and $36.49 before it. Why Piper cut was not reachable (the MSN 'nosediving' piece came back empty), so the cuts may reflect a real Q3 problem the print then confirms. That is why the size is small.
findings.independence: The price data is a separate source: Yahoo daily bars for LOB and KRE (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/LOB?range=3mo&interval=1d). The analyst actions and the EPS consensus both come from MarketBeat.

findings.finding: Credit was deteriorating going into Q3. Q2 2026 net charge-offs were $24.2M (0.80% annualised) against 0.63% in Q1, provision was $25.8M (up $5.7M QoQ), and nonperforming unguaranteed loans were $124.3M (1.00% of loans held for investment). The allowance fell to about 1.53% of HFI loans from 1.61% at year-end while loans grew 15.6% YoY. A Seeking Alpha piece of 2026-09-23 was titled 'Strong Growth, But Credit Risks Are Rising'. If Q3 provision or NCOs step up again, the EPS bar at about $0.66 is exposed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline carries a -13.96% reaction on the 2025-01-22 print, the only large move in the record. Its cause was not established in this search, and the 3 of 4 recent prints that rose all came with EPS beats despite rising provisions.
findings.why_not_priced: Q2 credit numbers are three months old and public, and the sell-side cuts plus the -11% de-rating probably already reflect a Q3 credit read. If credit were fully priced, the bar cut to FY $2.96 would leave room for a beat. If it were not, estimates would still sit near the pre-10-07 $3.07. They do not, so most of this is likely in the price. The finding is an inference from Q2 and does not rest on a Q3 number, and with about 10 days to cover a negative carries squeeze risk, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: The Seeking Alpha headline 'Live Oak Bancshares: Strong Growth, But Credit Risks Are Rising' (https://seekingalpha.com/article/4949027-live-oak-bancshares-strong-growth-but-credit-risks-are-rising, 2026-09-23) is the title only; the article body returned 403. The 10-Q balance sheet (allowance $193.4M on $12.63B HFI) comes from the same company data: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1462120/000146212026000058/lob-20260630.htm

findings.finding: The company's own release of 2026-10-19 says Live Oak was the top SBA 7(a) lender by dollar amount for SBA FY2026 (ended 2026-09-30), with 2,411 7(a) loans and more than $2.58B approved. That fiscal year covers calendar Q3 as its fourth quarter. The release gives no year-over-year comparison, so it shows production continued at scale but says nothing about direction for gain-on-sale.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 loan production was $1.548B (+13.2% QoQ) with gains on loan sales of $17.6M (+13.8% QoQ). The stock rose +3.9% on that print, together with the EPS beat.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public since 10-19, and the stock fell 1.32% that day, so the market did not read it as a positive surprise. The missing YoY comparison is the tell: had volume grown strongly the release would probably have said so. That caps it near zero either way.
findings.independence: The same release is mirrored on finviz (https://finviz.com/news/403950/live-oak-bank-named-nations-top-sba-7a-lender). No independent SBA series was reachable: the SBA report pages returned 404.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-20 at 16:20 ET, one day before the print, an 8-K Item 5.02 disclosed that Renato Derraik, Chief Information & Digital Officer of the bank, gave notice of resignation on 2026-10-14 'to pursue other endeavors', effective 2026-11-06, with no successor named.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No earlier officer-departure reaction was measured. The 2026-06-18 and 2026-07-02 5.02 filings came before a +3.9% print.
findings.why_not_priced: It was filed after the 10-20 close, and the stock is -0.7% intraday on 10-21 on light volume, so there has been little reaction. A tech/digital officer leaving is not on the line the stock trades on (EPS and credit), and the call may draw a question about it. It is worth close to nothing.

findings.finding: Insider selling clustered between the Q2 print and the end of the quarter: 17 Form 144 notices and 20 Form 4s from 2026-07-27 to 2026-09-11. Examples: CEO Mahan's trust sold 10,000 shares on each of 09-09 and 09-10 at about $38.6-38.7 under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2025-08-27; director W. Williams sold 6,590 at $40.09 on 09-03 (10b5-1); director T. Bradford sold 1,600 at $39.89 on 09-03 with no 10b5-1 flag. The sales were almost entirely pre-planned and small next to Mahan's holdings of about 6.2M shares.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured reaction to insider sales on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Form 4s are public and aggregated by insidertrades.com and MarketBeat. Because the sales are planned 10b5-1 trades, they carry little information about the quarter, and the one discretionary sale (1,600 shares) is trivial.
findings.independence: The Form 4 documents themselves: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1036743/000103674326000039/wk-form4_1789157131.xml and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1462120/000182458426000007/wk-form4_1788898706.xml (the same EDGAR record).

outside_window.finding: 8-K 8.01 of 2026-08-28: Chairman/CEO James S. Mahan III adopted a 10b5-1 plan to sell up to 400,000 voting common shares, with sales able to begin in November 2026 and run through November 2027. That is about 1.7 days of average volume, starting after the exit window.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The -5% 20-day and -19.5% from the high, together with the analyst cuts, mean the de-rating has already happened, which leans slightly against further downside and toward a lowered-bar beat. The single-source bar and the crowded short pull p_up back to about 51.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar single-sourced, finviz only): the lowered-bar finding was capped from +1.0 to +0.6 and p_up moved from 52 to 51, so the scaled number went from 0.18 to 0.09
Lessons 5 and 7 (an inference from Q2 credit, not a Q3 company number; about 10 days to cover): the credit finding was shrunk from -0.8 to -0.6
Lesson 3 (the finding's own caveat: no YoY comparison in the SBA release): the SBA finding was cut from +0.2 to +0.1
Lesson 3 (own caveat: planned 10b5-1 sales; a non-financial officer leaving): the insider cluster and the CIDO resignation were each cut from -0.2 to -0.1
Left standing: the CEO's 400k-share plan stays in outside_window (it starts in November), and abs_move_pct stays at 4.5 (median 3.9, raised for no options, thin coverage and a 10-day short)
